For example:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># make BATCH_DELETE_OLD_FILES=yes delete-old-libs</span></code></pre></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div><div class=sect3><h4 id=updating-src-completing-restart>27.7.6.3. Restarting After the Update<a class=anchor href=#updating-src-completing-restart></a></h4><div class=paragraph><p>The last step after updating is to restart the computer so all the changes take effect:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># shutdown -r now</span></code></pre></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class=sect1><h2 id=pkgbase>27.8. Updating FreeBSD with packages<a class=anchor href=#pkgbase></a></h2><div class=sectionbody><div class=paragraph><p>Starting from 14.0-RELEASE, the FreeBSD project has published a set of packages of the base system, using <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=pkg&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">pkg(8)</a>.
The convenience of pkg is no longer limited to the FreeBSD ports collection.
<a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=pkg&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">pkg(8)</a> can be used for FreeBSD itself.
Base packages, and usage thereof, were traditionally referred to as <em>pkgbase</em>.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>Publication of official packages began in <a href=https://lists.freebsd.org/archives/freebsd-pkgbase/2023-October/000221.html>October 2023</a>.
Their use with FreeBSD 14 is currently experimental.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>Starting from 15.0-RELEASE, <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=freebsd-base&amp;sektion=7&amp;format=html">freebsd-base(7)</a> will be supported as a tech preview for:</p></div><div class=ulist><ul><li><p>installation</p></li><li><p>minor upgrades</p></li><li><p>major upgrades</p></li></ul></div><div class=paragraph><p>freebsd-base will eventually replace:</p></div><div class=ulist><ul><li><p>tarball distribution sets, such as <code>base.txz</code> or <code>kernel.txz</code>, which are historically used for installation of the OS with <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=bsdinstall&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">bsdinstall(8)</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=freebsd-update&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">freebsd-update(8)</a> for updates to the OS.</p></li></ul></div><div class=paragraph><p>The current plan is for freebsd-update to work with pkg.</p></div><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>The replacement of distribution sets will take some time, until freebsd-base is fully stable!</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class=paragraph><p>Base System packages complement <a href=../cutting-edge/#makeworld>building and installing from source</a>, which is still available for those who wish to build their own custom kernels or userland.
It is also possible to build custom base system packages from local sources, as well as just relying on officially provided packages.</p></div><div class=sect2><h3 id=_converting_a_host_to_use_freebsd_base>27.8.1. Converting a Host to use freebsd-base<a class=anchor href=#_converting_a_host_to_use_freebsd_base></a></h3><div class=paragraph><p>FreeBSD 14.0-RELEASE or later can be converted to use base packages.
Earlier versions must be upgraded with freebsd-update before conversion.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>For conversion, the FreeBSD Foundation-sponsored <a href=https://github.com/FreeBSDFoundation/pkgbasify>pkgbasify</a> tool is recommended.
Follow the instructions given there.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p><a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=freebsd-update&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">freebsd-update(8)</a> will be enhanced to use pkg and pkgbasify.</p></div><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>Note that this migration requires up to 5GiB additional free space, to download, unpack, and relocate any conflicting files.
The pkgbasify tool does not check for this and it is the responsibility of the user to ensure that enough space is available before running the migration.</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class=paragraph><p><a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=pkgbasify&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">pkgbasify(8)</a> (or whatever outcome <a href=https://reviews.freebsd.org/D51594>D51594</a> or <a href=https://wiki.freebsd.org/WantedPorts#O-P>port request</a> will have) performs 6 main tasks:</p></div><div class=ulist><ul><li><p>Creates a backup boot environment (ZFS only) with <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=bectl&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">bectl(8)</a></p></li><li><p>Creates the new package repository config files</p></li><li><p>Upgrades existing system components such as base, kernel, lib32, debug</p></li><li><p>Merges existing and new config files</p></li><li><p>Updates passwd and capabilities databases</p></li><li><p>Restarts sshd immediately</p></li></ul></div></div><div class=sect2><h3 id=_upgrading_a_host_using_freebsd_base>27.8.2. Upgrading a Host using freebsd-base<a class=anchor href=#_upgrading_a_host_using_freebsd_base></a></h3><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>This is still in development, so please be careful especially when converting an existing system to use freebsd-base.</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class=paragraph><p>Create a folder for custom pkg repository config files, if there is none present already.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># mkdir -p /usr/local/etc/pkg/repos/</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>For using the freebsd-base repository, create a pkg repository configuration file called <code>FreeBSD-base.conf</code>:</p></div><div id=pgk-base-repo-configuration class="literalblock programlisting"><div class=content><pre>FreeBSD-base {
    url = &#34;pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_release_${VERSION_MINOR}&#34;;
    mirror_type = &#34;srv&#34;;
    signature_type = &#34;fingerprints&#34;;
    fingerprints = &#34;/usr/share/keys/pkg&#34;;
    enabled = yes;
}</pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>for more information on specific configuration options see <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=pkg.conf&amp;sektion=5&amp;format=html">pkg.conf(5)</a>.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>There are different branches to choose from (by changing the url accordingly):</p></div><table id=table-of-packagebase-branches class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch"><caption class=title>Table 2. Base system package Branches</caption><col style=width:10%><col style=width:20%><col style=width:70%><tbody><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>Branch</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>Frequency</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>URL</p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>main</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>twice daily - 12:00 and 00:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_latest</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>main</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>weekly – Sunday at 12:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_weekly</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>stable/14</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>twice daily – 12:00 and 00:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_latest</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>stable/14</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>weekly – Sunday at 12:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_weekly</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>releng/14.3</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>twice daily – 12:00 and 00:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_release_3</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>releng/15.0</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>twice daily – 12:00 and 00:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_release_0</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>stable/15</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>twice daily – 12:00 and 00:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_latest</code></p></td></tr><tr><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>stable/15</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock>weekly – Sunday at 12:00 UTC</p></td><td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class=tableblock><code>pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_weekly</code></p></td></tr></tbody></table><div class=paragraph><p>To upgrade the system, change the configuration file according to the desired release, and run:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># pkg update -r FreeBSD-base</span>
<span class=c># pkg upgrade -r FreeBSD-base</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>check, if these packages are correct and accept the changes.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>Reboot the OS executing the following command:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># shutdown -r now</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=sect3><h4 id=pkgbase-major-upgrade>27.8.2.1. Major Upgrades<a class=anchor href=#pkgbase-major-upgrade></a></h4><div class=paragraph><p>With ZFS, boot environments allow an upgrade to be performed without interrupting running software.
If the system does not use root-on-ZFS: backup before upgrading.</p></div><div class=sect4><h5 id=_preparations>Preparations<a class=anchor href=#_preparations></a></h5><div class=paragraph><p>Change <code>/usr/local/etc/pkg/repos/FreeBSD-base.conf</code> to target the correct major release like <code>base_release_0</code> for 15.0-RELEASE, to look like this:</p></div><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>This file might change to be included in RELEASE with a different path.</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class="literalblock programlisting"><div class=content><pre>FreeBSD-base {
    url = &#34;pkg+https://pkg.freebsd.org/${ABI}/base_release_0&#34;;
    mirror_type = &#34;srv&#34;;
    signature_type = &#34;fingerprints&#34;;
    fingerprints = &#34;/usr/share/keys/pkg&#34;;
    enabled = yes;
}</pre></div></div><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>As pkgbase with FreeBSD 14 is experimental, so is a pkgbase major upgrade to 15.
At the time of this writing in some edge-cases the major upgrade removes pkg and therefore segfaults.
This is considered a (<a href=https://github.com/freebsd/pkg/issues/2475>known issue</a>) for 15.0-RELEASE.
To work around this issue, lock pkg before upgrading.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># pkg -c /mnt/upgrade lock pkg</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>An experimental major upgrade from FreeBSD 14, to 15 (or 16.0-CURRENT), should be followed by installation of meta package <code>FreeBSD-set-minimal</code>.</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class=paragraph><p>Save a list of the non-base packages in case they are needed later:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell>pkg prime-origins | <span class=nb>sort</span> <span class=nt>-u</span> <span class=o>&gt;</span> /var/tmp/pkg-prime-origins.txt</code></pre></div></div></div><div class=sect4><h5 id=pkgbase-major-zfs>Major Upgrade With ZFS<a class=anchor href=#pkgbase-major-zfs></a></h5><div class=paragraph><p>Create a boot environment using <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=bectl&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">bectl(8)</a> and name it according to the version upgrading to</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># bectl create 15.0-RELEASE</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Create a directory then mount the new boot environment there to enable working with pkg <a href="https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=chroot&amp;sektion=8&amp;format=html">chroot(8)</a> and rootdir.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># mkdir /mnt/upgrade</span>
<span class=c># bectl mount 15.0-RELEASE /mnt/upgrade</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>The next step will upgrade the boot environment to the specified version.</p></div><div class="admonitionblock warning"><table><tbody><tr><td class=icon><i class="fa icon-warning" title=Warning></i></td><td class=content><div class=paragraph><p>This step might remove non-base packages, which could include the running desktop environment.</p></div></td></tr></tbody></table></div><div class=paragraph><p>Set the environment variable ABI to upgrade the major version (replace amd64 with the architecture and 15 with the targeted version).
Set the pkg-static chroot directory to the boot environment mountpoint.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># env ABI=FreeBSD:15:amd64 pkg-static -c /mnt/upgrade upgrade -r FreeBSD-base</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>There will be a prompt asking about ignoring the version mismatch looking like this:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell>Newer FreeBSD version <span class=k>for </span>package FreeBSD-zoneinfo:
To ignore this error <span class=nb>set </span><span class=nv>IGNORE_OSVERSION</span><span class=o>=</span><span class=nb>yes</span>
- package: 1500058
- running userland: 1500000
Ignore the mismatch and <span class=k>continue</span>? <span class=o>[</span>y/N]:</code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Check and confirm that.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>To check if that was successful, chroot into the mountpoint of the boot environment and run <code>freebsd-version -ku</code>.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># chroot /mnt/upgrade</span>
<span class=c># freebsd-version -ku</span>
<span class=c># exit</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Activate the boot environment temporarily and reboot.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># bectl activate -t 15.0-RELEASE</span>
<span class=c># shutdown -r now</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>If the system does not work as expected: restart the OS to cease using the temporarily active boot environment.
The next boot will reuse the pre-upgrade environment.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>If the system runs stable after reboot, don’t forget to permanently activate this boot environment to prevent accidentally booting the old system.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell>bectl activate 15.0-RELEASE</code></pre></div></div></div><div class=sect4><h5 id=pkgbase-major-non-zfs>Major Upgrade Without ZFS<a class=anchor href=#pkgbase-major-non-zfs></a></h5><div class=paragraph><p>Set the environment variable ABI to upgrade the major version (replace amd64 with the architecture and 15 with the targeted version).</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># env ABI=FreeBSD:15:amd64 pkg-static upgrade -r FreeBSD-base</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>There will be a prompt to ask about ignoring the version mismatch looking like this:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell>Newer FreeBSD version <span class=k>for </span>package FreeBSD-zoneinfo:
To ignore this error <span class=nb>set </span><span class=nv>IGNORE_OSVERSION</span><span class=o>=</span><span class=nb>yes</span>
- package: 1500058
- running userland: 1500000
Ignore the mismatch and <span class=k>continue</span>? <span class=o>[</span>y/N]:</code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Check and confirm that.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>To check if the upgrade was successful, run <code>freebsd-version -ku</code>.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>Then reboot.</p></div></div><div class=sect4><h5 id=_post_upgrade_tasks>Post-upgrade tasks<a class=anchor href=#_post_upgrade_tasks></a></h5><div class=paragraph><p>If pkg was locked during the update as a workaround remove the lock like this:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># pkg unlock pkg</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>After upgrading to a new major version, updates and upgrades of installed packages to match the ABI version may be necessary.</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># pkg upgrade</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Consider getting help from <a href=https://www.freebsd.org/support/>FreeBSD Support</a> when experiencing issues.</p></div></div></div></div><div class=sect2><h3 id=build-pkgbase-packages-locally>27.8.3. Manually building pkgbase and publishing it to the local network<a class=anchor href=#build-pkgbase-packages-locally></a></h3><div class=paragraph><p>When building custom pkgbase packages clone the FreeBSD source tree:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># cd /usr/src</span>
<span class=c># git clone https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src.git /usr/src</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Check out the branch for the release to build packages for:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># git checkout releng/14.3</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>Start the building process, depending on the resources available this could take some while.
Set the parallel processes according to the CPU core count.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>This example is written for an 8 core CPU:</p></div><div class=listingblock><div class=content><pre class="rouge highlight"><code data-lang=shell><span class=c># make -j8 buildworld &amp;&amp; make -j8 buildkernel &amp;&amp; make -j8 packages</span></code></pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>When building frequently, consider using <a href=https://cgit.freebsd.org/ports/tree/devel/ccache/>devel/ccache</a> to speed up subsequent builds from the cache.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>After building, the packages will get saved into <code>/usr/obj/usr/src/repo/FreeBSD:14:amd64/14.3p2</code> or something like that, depending on the version build.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>To publish these packages to the network set up a nginx service and use this location in the http server configuration:</p></div><div class="literalblock programlisting"><div class=content><pre> location /FreeBSD:14:amd64 {
   alias /usr/obj/usr/src/repo/FreeBSD:14:amd64/;
   autoindex on;
 }</pre></div></div><div class=paragraph><p>And reload the nginx service.</p></div><div class=paragraph><p>When not using https, use a small configuration file on the clients to target the pkgbase version just built by editing <code>/usr/local/etc/pkg/repos/upgrade.conf</code>:</p></div><div class="literalblock programlisting"><div class=content><pre>upgrade: {
	url         = http://ip.of.the.server/FreeBSD:14:amd64/14.3p2
	enabled     = yes
